speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I understand you are experiencing postmenopausal bleeding and have been found to have an adnexal mass. To help determine the cause, can you describe the amount and frequency of the bleeding, and have you noticed any associated abdominal pain or bloating?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any pelvic pain, pressure, or bloating, and do you have a family history of breast or ovarian cancer? I would also like to examine you to assess the size and characteristics of the adnexal mass.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying that. To better characterize the adnexal mass and rule out malignancy, I need to see the imaging details. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Thickened endometrial stripe and left adnexal mass observed

speaker: Doctor
text: The thickened endometrial stripe raises concern for endometrial pathology, so I need to rule out cancer directly. REQUEST TEST: Endometrial_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms endometrial adenocarcinoma, but we must determine if the adnexal mass is a separate ovarian malignancy or a metastasis. REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal CA-125 levels and well-differentiated histology, the adnexal mass is likely a benign ovarian lesion coincident with early-stage endometrial cancer. DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial adenocarcinoma with coincident benign ovarian mass
